subject: Request: Subprocessor cascade + Order Form amendment (Acme Logistics)
messages:
From: m.sanchez <m.sanchez@acme-logistics.com>
To: ava_chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-logistics.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor cascade + Order Form amendment request

Hi Ava / Dev team,

Quick note from Acme procurement: we are adding a new analytics provider (CloudMetrics LLC) that will process a subset of telemetry derived from our integrations. Our security team flagged that the current Order Form and MSA do not explicitly flow down subprocessor obligations for this kind of telemetry (retention, access controls, certs).

Attached is a proposed Order Form amendment and a high-level subprocessor matrix. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept a vendor flow-down that includes: (1) data processing limitation to aggregate telemetry only, (2) SOC2 Type II evidence for CloudMetrics, and (3) a one-year retention limit with quarterly audit rights.

We need a response for our internal approval loop by end of day Tuesday. If any of this requires an Order Form addendum or MSA redline, please indicate the expected timeline.

Thanks,
Martin Sanchez
Sr. Procurements Manager
Acme Logistics

Attachments: acme_orderform-amendment-request.pdf, subprocessor_matrix_v2.xlsx

From: ava_chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: m.sanchez <m.sanchez@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor cascade + Order Form amendment request

Martin — thanks for the heads-up and the attachments. Looping in Dev to confirm technical constraints and Legal/Product (Lauren) for terms.

Plan from our side:
- Dev (Dev) will confirm whether the telemetry is covered by our current processing definitions and whether we can isolate/aggregate before sending to CloudMetrics.
- Legal (Lauren) will review the requested flow-down language and advise whether we can accept the three bullets as-is or propose suitable alternative phrasing.
- Ops (Jonas) will check whether SOC2 evidence from CloudMetrics is sufficient and whether we can request an addendum for audit rights.

Action items: Lauren, can you review the attached redline request and send back a short list of required changes and an estimated review time? Dev — confirm technical feasibility today if possible. Martin — thanks for the timeline; we will prioritize.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: ava_chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: m.sanchez <m.sanchez@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor cascade + Order Form amendment request

Thanks Ava — I reviewed the two attachments and sketched a stop-gap redline (attached: redline_notes_for_legal.docx). High-level comments below:

- "Aggregate telemetry only": We can commit to sending only aggregated telemetry to CloudMetrics, but we should define what "aggregate" means (minimum group size / no PII / hashed identifiers). I propose a short definition clause in the Order Form amendment.
- "SOC2 Type II evidence": Acceptable, but we need CloudMetrics to provide an up-to-date audit report and a certificate URL. Recommend adding a clause that Redwood may accept equivalent attestations (ISO 27001, or an SSAE report) subject to approval.
- "One-year retention + quarterly audit rights": Quarterly on-site audits are excessive for a pure analytics subprocessor. Suggest: annual attestations plus right to request evidence on a quarterly basis with reasonable notice. If Acme insists on quarterly, Legal will need to escalate for exec sign-off.

Timeline: I can produce a redline to our standard Order Form amendment and the MSA clause by EOD Monday (Mar 15) if this is purely standard language. If Acme requires quarterly on-site audit rights as written, I will need to escalate and estimate 3–5 business days thereafter.

Attaching: redline_notes_for_legal.docx (staging changes, suggested phrasing).

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_notes_for_legal.docx

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: ava_chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: m.sanchez <m.sanchez@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor cascade + Order Form amendment request

Quick tech update: CloudMetrics will only receive pre-aggregated metrics (no raw logs). We can implement the aggregation boundary in the pipeline and drop any upstream identifiers. Estimated deployment window: 3 business days to configure and validate for the Acme integration. No change to latency or throughput expected.

I also confirmed we can tag telemetry with a "no-PII" label and generate a weekly export to the subprocessor with retention enforced on our side (we will enforce deletion after 12 months).

Dev

Martin / Acme procurement —

Thanks for the patience. Summary and next steps:

1) Tech: Redwood can isolate and deliver only aggregated metrics to CloudMetrics; implementation window 3 business days (Dev will own).
2) Legal: We will provide a redlined Order Form amendment and an MSA clause defining "aggregate telemetry" and acceptable evidence for subprocessor SOC2/ISO by EOD Monday (Mar 15).
3) Audit cadence: Redwood proposes annual attestations + ad-hoc evidence requests with 15 business days' notice. If Acme requires quarterly audit rights as a hard term, please indicate explicitly so we can escalate.

Please confirm whether the proposed audit cadence is acceptable. If so, we will route the redlined docs and a DocuSign package for signature. If Acme needs quarterly audits, we will need to start an exec approval path and will advise timelines.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
